features.name: Calculator
features.summary: A stateless arithmetic library exposing four exact-decimal operations.

returns.description: Static class; it is never instantiated.

behaviors.statement: The assembly is a class library and exposes no entry point.
All operations are pure: they hold no state and mutate nothing between calls.

invariants.statement: Every operation uses exact decimal arithmetic, never binary floating point, so decimal fractions are represented without rounding drift.

features.name: Add
features.summary: Returns the sum of the two operands.

returns.description: The exact sum of left and right.

behaviors.statement: Returns the arithmetic sum of the two operands.
Negative operands are supported and follow ordinary signed arithmetic.
Adding zero returns the other operand unchanged.

errors.condition: the sum cannot be represented as a 96-bit coefficient at any scale from the operands' scale down to 0. The addends are first aligned to a common scale, reducing it (with rounding to nearest, ties away from zero) until both fit; an excess that vanishes under that reduction returns decimal.MaxValue rather than throwing, so decimal.MaxValue + 0.1 is MaxValue while decimal.MaxValue + 1 throws

invariants.statement: Decimal precision is preserved exactly: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3, not a binary-float approximation of it.

features.name: Subtract
features.summary: Returns the difference of the two operands, left minus right.

behaviors.statement: Returns left minus right; operand order is significant.
A result smaller than zero is returned as a negative value rather than clamped.
Subtracting two negative operands follows ordinary signed arithmetic.

errors.condition: the difference cannot be represented as a 96-bit coefficient at any scale from the operands' scale down to 0; as with addition the operands are aligned with rounding to nearest, ties away from zero, so an excess that vanishes under that reduction returns the boundary value rather than throwing

invariants.statement: Fractional operands keep their exact scale: 3.75 - 2.5 is 1.25.

features.name: Multiply
features.summary: Returns the product of the two operands.

returns.description: The exact product of left and right.

behaviors.statement: Returns the arithmetic product of the two operands.
The sign of the result follows the signs of the operands.

errors.condition: the product cannot be represented even after reducing its scale to 0 -- that is, its integer part needs more than a 96-bit coefficient (decimal.MaxValue * 1.1 throws, while decimal.MaxValue * 1.0 does not). A product too small to represent does not throw: it rounds to 0

invariants.statement: A decimal is a 96-bit unsigned coefficient scaled by a power of ten, with the scale constrained to 0-28; these are two independent limits and either one can force rounding. The product's ideal scale is the sum of the operand scales (1.25 * 2.5 is exactly 3.125, scale 3). When the exact product would need a coefficient wider than 96 bits, the scale is reduced -- rounding the value to nearest, ties away from zero -- until the coefficient fits, even if the reduced scale is far below the sum: decimal.MaxValue * 0.11 has operand scales summing to 2 but returns 8715097876569077135289834537 at scale 0. When the ideal scale exceeds 28 the result is rounded to scale 28 instead, which is why 1e-28 * 1e-28 returns 0 rather than overflowing or preserving scale. Only when no scale down to 0 admits a representable coefficient does the operation throw.

features.name: Divide
features.summary: Returns the quotient of dividend divided by divisor, rejecting a zero divisor.

behaviors.statement: Returns dividend divided by divisor; operand order is significant.
The quotient is not truncated to an integer: 5 / 2 is 2.5, not 2.
The sign of the quotient follows the signs of the operands.
A zero dividend with a non-zero divisor returns zero rather than throwing.

errors.condition: divisor is zero, for any dividend including zero and negatives
errors.result: DivideByZeroException with message 'Cannot divide by zero.'

errors.condition: the quotient's integer part needs more than a 96-bit coefficient, so no scale down to 0 can represent it, such as decimal.MaxValue / 0.1

invariants.statement: The zero-divisor check precedes the division, so the operation never relies on hardware division-by-zero behaviour.
